key_insight: GeoThinker replaces passive, global fusion of 3D geometry with an active perception strategy that selectively queries and integrates task-relevant geometric cues, improving alignment between semantic and geometric information for spatial reasoning.
problem_solved: Existing MLLM approaches expose 3D geometry as a single, indiscriminate feature stream, which creates semantic–geometry misalignment and redundant signals that degrade spatial reasoning performance and efficiency.
method: Active perception loop: a learnable controller selectively queries the 3D encoder for task-relevant geometric cues rather than consuming a global geometry stream.
Selective integration: fuse only aligned geometric features with semantic features to reduce redundancy and improve correspondence between language and spatial structure.
Alignment-driven training: optimize cross-modal alignment objectives so geometry is interpreted in a task-aware, semantically grounded way.
impact: By making geometry integration selective and task-aware, GeoThinker yields more accurate and efficient spatial reasoning in multimodal systems, helping practitioners build MLLMs that better understand 3D scenes with fewer redundant features.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing passive fusion (global stream → model) vs. GeoThinker’s active loop (controller → selective queries → fused features).
Before/after illustrations: semantic–geometry misalignment hotspots vs. corrected alignment overlays on an image+point-cloud.
Attention/query visualization: heatmaps showing which geometric regions are queried for a given spatial reasoning question.
Performance schematic: compact bar or radar chart summarizing gains in accuracy, efficiency, and redundancy reduction (conceptual, not specific numbers).
paper_title: Thinking with Geometry: Active Geometry Integration for Spatial Reasoning
paper_authors: Haoyuan Li, Qihang Cao, Tao Tang, Kun Xiang, Zihan Guo
